headline: ECB vice president says rapid AI expansion could threaten financial stability
body: ECB Vice President Boris Vujčić said AI stock market valuations remain stretched and the risk of a repricing has risen. He added that "AI-related risks to system-wide stability now stem from a range of additional factors," pointing to the expansion of external funding from equity to debt markets, concentration of exposures, quickening AI adoption and potential cyberattacks.
note: In the same remarks, Vujčić flagged private credit, where rapid growth warrants close monitoring given limited transparency and growing interconnectedness with banks and insurers.

evidence.text: A European Central Bank official is warning that rapid artificial intelligence (AI) expansion could threaten the region’s financial stability.
AI stock market valuations remain stretched and the risk of a repricing has risen, European Central Bank Vice President Boris Vujčić said Monday (Nov. 16).

“AI-related risks to system-wide stability now stem from a range of additional factors,” he added, also pointing to “the expansion of external funding from equity to debt markets, concentration of exposures, quickening AI adoption and potential cyberattacks.”

While risks currently appear contained, the rapid growth of private credit warrants close monitoring, given limited transparency, growing interconnectedness with banks and insurers, and potential liquidity mismatches,” he said.
